issues.description: Test for invalid POST relies on backend's behavior when stream short-reads but doesn't assert on root cause
issues.detail: resp4 sends empty body with Content-Length: 1. The example reads bounded_stream which should return empty bytes, triggering 'Empty request body' (400). However, the test doesn't verify which 400 path was hit (auth vs JSON vs empty). Asserting status_code alone is fragile; consider asserting the title/description so a future regression doesn't pass silently.

issues.description: FAQ example uses unbounded req.stream.read(req.content_length) which can hang or misbehave
issues.detail: The FAQ snippet says clients should call req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0). With WSGI, req.stream may not be bounded; reading client-supplied length unguarded is exactly the pattern the example PR is trying to fix elsewhere by switching to bounded_stream. The FAQ teaches the anti-pattern.

issues.description: FAQ test example has incorrect TestClient construction signature
issues.detail: falcon.testing.TestClient does not exist as a public API in the form shown; the canonical helper is falcon.testing.TestClient(app) only in newer versions, but the docs elsewhere typically use simulate_* on app or TestClient(app). Verify against current falcon API or users copy-pasting will hit ImportError/AttributeError.

issues.description: FAQ code style uses redundant tuple and unidiomatic assert
issues.detail: headers = [('Content-Length', '1'),] has an unnecessary trailing comma making it a list of one tuple when a dict is more idiomatic and matches the rest of the FAQ. assert(result.status == ...) uses parens around the expression which is a common pylint warning (assert is a statement). Minor doc polish.

issues.description: README diff includes unrelated signature change to StorageError.handle
issues.detail: The README example reorders StorageError.handle parameters from (ex, req, resp, params) to (req, resp, ex, params). This is a substantive API-shape change unrelated to the PR's stated goal of adding POST tests. If intentional (matching falcon error handler signature change), it deserves its own changelog note; if accidental, it confuses readers.

issues.description: Switching to bounded_stream changes behavior for clients sending no Content-Length
issues.detail: req.bounded_stream returns an empty read when Content-Length is missing, where req.stream.read() previously would read what's available. For chunked transfer encoding or missing Content-Length, valid JSON bodies will now be silently treated as empty and produce a 400. Worth a note in the example comments.

review.summary: The PR adds reasonable POST test coverage and a FAQ entry, but the FAQ example teaches a potentially unsafe stream-read pattern and uses minor unidiomatic Python. The test for the invalid POST asserts only on status code, which could mask regressions where a different 400 path fires. The README has an unrelated parameter-order change to StorageError.handle that warrants explanation. Switching to bounded_stream in the example is the right call but has subtle behavioral implications for missing Content-Length that aren't documented.
